Check the file of to_one_file() on this computer

Source: R/one_file_check.R
check_one_file.Rd

check_one_file() runs the file <version>_one_file.R of the project in a new R session, on copies of the folders of the project. It prints PASS when the real results are those of the project, or else the first difference.

Usage

check_one_file(...)

Arguments

...

Nothing. A call with an argument stops. check_one_file() takes the version and the paths of the server from the last initialize_project() of this R session.

Value

Invisibly, TRUE on PASS and FALSE on FAIL.

Details

Run the project as normal first, so that <version>_results/real/ holds its real results. Write the file with to_one_file(), and call initialize_project() again in this R session, with one_file_home and one_file_folders.

check_one_file() then does these steps:

  1. It makes the lines of to_one_file() in memory, with the code of the project and the paths of the server of the last initialize_project(). It compares them with <version>_one_file.R in the project, line by line. This R session is the one source of the paths, so a change of one_file_home in the run script also makes the file older. Only the line of the header with the version of pbn and the date does not count. When a line differs, the file is older than the code of the project. It prints FAIL with the number of the first line that differs and the line in both files, each cut to 80 characters. It says to run to_one_file() again. A file of an older pbn, with the argument one_file, also gets this FAIL, and the text says so. It prints FAIL also when the project has no such file.

  2. Without real results, it stops here. So the file of a project MAY be checked for ASCII, for a parse and for a left-out function before the first full run.

  3. It compares manifest$source_md5 of the real results with the md5 of the files of the project now, without <version>_functions/blocks.R. When they differ, the results of the project are older than its code. It prints FAIL with the changed files and says to run <version>_run.R again. It runs nothing.

  4. It makes a temporary folder with an empty project folder, and a copy of each folder of the project with all its files. The empty project folder stands for the server, where there is no functions folder and no pbn.yml.

  5. It writes a copy of the file of the project to the temporary folder. In the copy, each line with a path of the server gets the temporary path. These are the lines where to_one_file() with the temporary paths writes another line. It runs the copy with Rscript in a new R session. So the check runs the file that goes into git.

  6. It compares results.qs2 and results_gitexclude.qs2 of the real results of the run with those of the project, element by element.

  7. It calls each block of show_block() on the real results of the project and on those of the run, in one more new R session. That session attaches no package of the run script. It compares what show_block() prints for each page of each block, as text, without the line FAKE REAL DATA. A block that stops on either results, or that prints other text, is a FAIL that names the block.

Four fields of the manifest MAY differ, and the comparison leaves them out:

  • run_date, the date of the run.

  • packages, the loaded packages, because the new R session loads other packages than the R session of the normal run.

  • the column from_cache of data_cache, because the copy has no cache.

  • fake_real_data, because the file never runs on fake real data. See initialize_project().

The comparison also leaves <version>_functions/blocks.R out of source_md5, also for results of an older pbn that hold it. Every other element MUST be identical, also source_md5, data_files and cache_key. So the results do not depend on the place of the project and of its folders. The copies keep the modification times of the files, with file.copy(copy.date = TRUE). That is why data_files and the cache key agree. pbn reads no content of a data file, so a copy with new times looks like changed data. The times are whole seconds, so a copy that loses a part of a second, as on Windows, still agrees.

When the run of the file stops with an error, check_one_file() prints FAIL with the exit status and the last 20 lines of the output of the run, and compares nothing. On PASS, it deletes the temporary folder. On FAIL, it keeps it, and the text names the folder with the file and the output of its run.

The check copies each folder, so it needs the disk space of the real data once more. These are its limits:

  • It cannot check what differs on the server, for example the versions of R and of the packages there.

  • It runs the file with Rscript, and on the server a person pastes it into an interactive R session. So it does not cover code that depends on interactive().

  • It compares the blocks on the real data of this computer. A block that stops only on other data, for example on an empty table, passes here.

  • pbn reads no content of a data file. A data file that changed in place and kept its size and its modification time is not seen.

See also

vignette("pbn"), section "Running on an air-gapped server".
